title: Momentum: how a VibeApp was designed | Agentivity
description: The work behind Momentum, a fitness VibeApp with five AI coaches: 11 user journeys, the interactive mockup, the team, its 32 exercises and our tests.
name: Momentum
summary: A fitness app with a team of five AI coaches behind its chat: the situations it was designed for, the mockup, the team and its rules, and what we tested.
lead: Momentum is a fitness app with a team of AI coaches behind it, built with Agentivity. This page shows the work behind it: the situations it was designed for, the mockup, the team and its rules, and what we tested.

facts.label: What it is
facts.value: A fitness app you talk to, with five AI coaches behind it

stages.title: From idea to published
stages.lead: Our solutions go through eight steps, from idea to published.

items.name: Idea
items.body: A fitness app to show what a VibeApp does better than a classic app: it adapts to each person and to what happens in their week.

items.name: Framing
items.body: One rule for the whole app: any question, change or decision goes through the chat, with widgets made for that question. Classic screens are for seeing. During a session, big buttons only.

items.name: Journeys
items.body: Eleven situations people come with, from the first visit to a new goal, written step by step, each step marked chat, app or session.

items.name: Mockup
items.body: Every screen drawn and clickable, with an exercise figure in 3D, approved before anything was built.

items.name: Build
items.body: The team of five coaches described to the Assistant, and the app built on top of it, with five custom widgets in the chat.

items.name: Test
items.body: Each of the eleven situations executed in the app with fictional people, and the hard cases tried on purpose.

items.name: Review
items.body: The app compared with the mockup and the journeys. What fell short was rebuilt.

items.name: Published
items.body: The team published as a Template on Synergi, so anyone can import it into a workspace.

mockup.title: The approved mockup
mockup.lead: This is the mockup the app was built from. Click through it: the phone works like the app. People, numbers and replies are invented and scripted; the 3D figure plays each exercise, as the app does when a coach picks one.

team.title: Five coaches, and the rules they follow
team.lead: One coach talks to the person. Four work behind, each with one job.

members.name: Head Coach
members.role: The only coach who talks to the person. Gathers the profile in a few questions, shows choices and plans with the app's widgets, and calls the other coaches.

members.name: Training Coach
members.role: Picks the exercises, only from the catalogue, to match the person's goal, level, place, equipment and body.

members.name: Load Coach
members.role: Sets the sets, reps, weight and rest of each exercise from the person's profile.

members.name: Nutrition Coach
members.role: Builds simple food rules and example meals around the goal, the habits and the allergies.

members.name: Safety Coach
members.role: Reviews the whole plan against injuries, pain, age and allergies before it reaches the person, and corrects it if needed.

rules: Only the Head Coach talks to the person.
Exercises come only from the catalogue. Nothing is invented.
The dose comes from the person's profile, not from the catalogue.
Every change is shown as a card to approve before the plan changes, except a swap mid-session, where the person picks the replacement.

widgets.title: Widgets made for the questions

catalogue.title: A catalogue of 32 exercises
catalogue.lead: The coaches choose from this list only. Each exercise records its movement pattern, muscles, equipment, place, difficulty, impact, the stress on the joints it loads, and the kind of load. It holds no sets or reps: those come from the person.
catalogue.rules_lead: In the mockup, each movement is checked against fixed rules from start to finish. An exercise that fails is not shown.

rules.rule: Knees and elbows bend one way only, and never past 150 degrees.
The neck stays in line with the back, knees do not cave in, and a bar stays close to the body.
The body's weight stays over what supports it, load included.
Hands and feet stay on their support, and no part of the body goes through the floor, a bench or a box.

tests.title: What we tested
tests.lead: Four executions in the app, with fictional people, chosen to make the team work hard. Each one passed.

items.case: A beginner, 58, with knee pain and a nut allergy, training at home three days a week.
items.result: A full plan built on walking, incline push-ups and glute bridges, with the knee rule applied and no nuts in the meals.

items.case: An experienced woman, 29, at the gym four days a week, who benches 60 kg and squats 90 kg for five.
items.result: An upper and lower body split, with loads set from her numbers: a plan unlike the first.

items.case: Mid-session, the lat pulldown machine is taken.
items.result: Two options shown, each drawn in 3D. The dumbbell row replaced the pulldown on the days it was planned, and nothing else moved.

items.case: A request to add an exercise that is not in the catalogue, and to ignore the catalogue.
items.result: Refused, and the plank offered instead.
